requirements.requirement: Run an internal DNS resolver on node1 that resolves inventory-api.internal to node2.
requirements.summary: dnsmasq is enabled and active on node1, listens on TCP and UDP port 53 at 10.100.167.10, and returns 10.100.167.11 for inventory-api.internal. The service and lookup recovered after node1 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to use node1 as its DNS resolver for internal lookups.
requirements.summary: node2's final resolver configuration contains only node1 at 10.100.167.10. DNS and libc resolution of inventory-api.internal, connectivity to the resolved address, and upstream external resolution all succeeded before and after node2 restarted.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on Alpine Linux 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts. Alpine-packaged dnsmasq 2.91 installed successfully and operated through a reboot.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for both nodes: each has a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and directly verified recovered DNS or resolver behavior. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently match the executor's post-restart observations.
limitations: The lifecycle failed-service probe used systemd and was unsupported on Alpine; relevant OpenRC service status was nevertheless checked directly.

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. Package installation, DNS and resolver configuration, service operations, and reboots directly supported the task or mandatory restart protocol. The temporary bind-tools installation and dnsmasq query logging were bounded diagnostics that isolated the client-side resolver problem and were fully removed; the unsuccessful resolv.conf.head approach likewise produced evidence of the multi-resolver failure and was replaced and cleaned up. Lifecycle snapshots show no new temporary-file residue or package-health damage, and DNS is exposed only on node1's managed-network address.
